body.statement: Using \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{enum}}\), can one construct an output-polynomial or polynomial-delay algorithm that emits each distinct rational total-effect functional \(g_E\), for \(E\in\mathcal R(C)\), exactly once and returns a certificate partitioning all states by functional equality, while preserving the shortest legal-reversal certificates from \(C\)? The construction must derive path independence of transported partitions and may not assume that numerically coincident evaluations identify equal rational functionals.
body.justification: State enumeration can be exponentially more redundant than the causal output, and symbolic duplicate removal is the nonroutine bridge from a structural class to usable possible-effect analysis.
body.gap: WienobstBannachLiskiewicz2023 counts ordinary Markov-equivalent DAGs by clique-picking, and GuoPerkovic2022EfficientLS estimates effects for enumerated parent sets; neither quotients a transported-partition component by equality of rational effect maps.
body.consumer: Large sparse components could feed IDA-style effect analysis without storing every observationally equivalent blocked state.
